config.purpose: H1: small CNN trained from scratch versus the Dense baseline of 04, same photos and seeds, with a shorter epoch limit for CNN

parameter_matching.reference: Dense baseline of 04 (986537 trainable parameters with 25 classes)
parameter_matching.note: Parameters are matched, operations are not: the CNN performs many more multiply-adds per image. Both are reported.

h1.question: Does spatial weight sharing help? CNN without BatchNorm versus Dense without dropout

batchnorm.question: Does BatchNorm help the same CNN? Only BatchNorm changes

config.phase_order: h1 first; batchnorm only after h1 results are saved
config.normalization: same RGB64 per-channel train moments as 04 (shared cache)
config.checkpoint: maximum validation macro-F1; first epoch wins ties
config.early_stopping: stop after 5 successive epochs without validation loss decreasing; different from checkpoint selection
config.primary_analysis: all three seeds; paired by seed with the Dense baseline of 04; no selection of best seed
config.test_policy: do not load or evaluate test images in this notebook

cost_feasibility.decision: Measure one real epoch per phase. Train only if the conservative estimate for three seeds fits the phase budget; otherwise stop for an explicit amendment. Never cap photos automatically.
cost_feasibility.amendment: Before CNN training, the H1 CPU pilot measured 166.7 seconds per epoch. Both CNN phases use at most 10 epochs per seed and a 110-minute pilot budget per phase. The Dense reference keeps its 30-epoch limit.

scope_limits: no width, depth, kernel or optimizer search
augmentation (H2) and class weights (H4) are studied in 09
validation is used for stopping and selection, so these are not final unbiased estimates
evaluation describes the selected garment types after quality controls, not the whole catalogue

normalization.method: population pixel moments after RGB64 Lanczos resize
